name: Holy Societates
description: Traditions that teach Holy Magic as a favored Ability, typically associated with the Order of Hermes, which can train Gifted and unGifted holy magi.

name: Sol Invictus
description: A holy societas descended from a Roman monotheistic sun cult worshipping Deus Sol Invictus; its Gifted members joined House Jerbiton and practice holy magic in 1220.

name: Deus Sol Invictus
description: The 'unconquered sun', the name of the one God worshipped by the Sol Invictus cult, proclaimed official deity of Rome under Elagabalus and Aurelian.

name: Holy Magic
description: Supernatural capacity for magic aligned with the Divine; Holy Societates teach it as a favored Ability and it is required to adopt a holy societas.

name: Cursing
description: A holy power Ability listed among the favored Abilities of Sol Invictus.

name: Ceremony
description: A holy power Ability listed among the favored Abilities of Sol Invictus.

name: Invocation
description: A holy power Ability listed among the favored Abilities of Sol Invictus.

name: Order of Hermes
description: The order of Hermetic magi; Holy Societates are typically associated with it, and the Church has no unified opinion of it.

name: House Jerbiton
description: Hermetic House which invited Gifted Invicti to join during the expansion following the Founding.

name: Cult of Mercury
description: A pagan cult, unfriendly to the Invicti, whose disintegration parallels the founding of the Order of Hermes.

name: The Gift
description: The inborn capacity for Hermetic magic; several Invicti possessed it and joined the Order.

name: Elagabalus
description: Roman emperor who declared Sol Invictus the State religion in the early third century and was removed four years later.

name: Aurelian
description: Roman emperor from 270, son of a Sol priestess, who proclaimed Deus Sol Invictus the official deity and built a temple and college in Rome.

name: Constantine
description: Roman emperor who supported Sol Invictus early, then converted to Christianity after seeing a glowing cross in 312 and made it the Empire's religion.

name: Plutarch
description: Ancient writer who told of a seer proclaiming that 'Great Pan is dead'.

name: Pan
description: Pagan god whose reported death convinced Romans their gods were not immortal.

name: Emesa
description: Syrian city where the Sol cultists kept a hidden temple with relics from Elagabalus' reign; liberated by Crusaders in 1110.

name: Rome
description: Seat of the pope and center of Christ's Church; site of Aurelian's sun temple and where the Invicti revived services.

name: Divine Realm
description: The realm of power of God; Sol Invictus is aligned with it and theologians associate Purgatory with it.

name: Infernal Realm
description: The realm of Hell and demons, recognized by the Invicti; some suggest Purgatory is a lesser circle of it.

name: Magic Realm
description: Realm of power recognized by the Invicti as distinct from Faerie and Infernal.

name: Faerie Realm
description: Realm of the fay; the Invicti must molest faeries, a Hermetic crime, and faerie powers may ignore Dominion penalties during Christmas.

name: Dominion
description: The Divine aura of Christian civilization, which lowers on holiday eves, is reduced by interdiction, and can be tempered by holy influence.

name: Holy Church
description: The Christian Church, the most influential institution in Mythic Europe, divided into secular and regular clergy and between Latin West and Greek East.

name: Christianity
description: The dominant religion of Mythic Europe in 1220, shaping every aspect of mundane society.

name: Jesus Christ
description: The Son of God, crucified, resurrected and ascended into heaven, whose life is commemorated by Christian holy days.

name: Shepherd of Hermas
description: Early Christian text (c. 140 A.D.) quoted describing a vision of the Church as an aged lady.

name: Hermas
description: Narrator of the Shepherd of Hermas who has a vision of the Church as an aged lady.

name: Sibyl
description: Figure Hermas mistakenly believes the aged woman of his vision to be.

name: Ars Notoria
description: The Notory Art of King Solomon; a Supernatural (also Academic and Arcane) Ability reciting orations called the Rings of Solomon.

name: King Solomon
description: Biblical king from whom the Christian rituals of wisdom and learning of Ars Notoria are handed down.

name: Pope Innocent III
description: Pope who opened the Fourth Lateran Council in 1215, placed England under interdict in 1208, and declared a Crusade against the Cathars in 1209.

name: Fourth Lateran Council
description: Church council of 1215 ruling that every Christian must take penance and the Eucharist yearly or be excommunicated.

name: Mythic Europe
description: The Ars Magica setting of Europe in 1220 A.D., essentially Christendom.

name: Jerusalem
description: Holy city where the Church began at Pentecost; taken by the First Crusade and recaptured by Saladin in 1187.

name: Twelve Apostles
description: The apostles who spread the story of Jesus Christ after Pentecost.

name: St. Paul
description: Apostle whose letters form part of the New Testament; greater saint and patron of Greece.

name: St. John the Evangelist
description: Apostle whose apocalyptic revelations close the New Testament; greater saint and patron of Asia Minor, friendship, and writers.

name: The Bible
description: Christian Scriptures of Old and New Testaments; a Summa on Theology (Level 10, Quality 3) and Church Lore (Level 3, Quality 3).

name: Easter
description: The most important Christian holy day, celebrating Christ's resurrection, on the first Sunday after the first full moon after the spring equinox.

name: Palm Sunday
description: The Sunday before Easter, recognizing Jesus' arrival in Jerusalem.

name: Good Friday
description: Day of mourning commemorating Christ's death on the cross.

name: Lent
description: Forty-day season of fasting before Easter, sometimes thought of as a spiritual tithe.

name: Pentecost
description: Celebration fifty days after Easter of the Holy Ghost appearing to the apostles; also called Whitsunday.

name: All Saints' Day
description: Feast on 1 November remembering all the saints.

name: All Hallows' Eve
description: Eve of All Saints' Day, reputed particularly evil as spirits and demons tempt those outdoors.

name: Christmas
description: Feast of Christ's nativity on December 25, beginning a twelve-day holy season during which realm boundaries blur.

name: Epiphany
description: Feast on January 6 of the Apparition of the Magi, ending the Christmas season.

name: Holy Innocents Day
description: December 28 feast when children are sometimes allowed to run the Church.

name: Feast of Fools
description: Celebration on January 1 reversing traditional roles such as bishop and jester.

name: Natalis Invicti
description: Day honoring the sun god's birth (December 25), adopted for the celebration of Christ's birth.

name: Holy War
description: Christian doctrine of religiously sanctioned war, developing from Augustine's just war into crusade doctrine.

name: St. Augustine of Hippo
description: Church father (354-430) who enunciated a theory of just war and wrote The City of God.

name: Pope Gregory VII
description: Pope (d. 1085) who enunciated a holy war theory underlying the Crusade.

name: Pope Urban II
description: Pope who preached the First Crusade at the Council of Clermont in 1095.

name: Council of Clermont
description: 1095 council where Urban II called for the First Crusade.

name: Crusades
description: Church-sanctioned holy wars to regain the Holy Land, of which four have struck by 1220.

name: First Crusade
description: Crusade from 1095 that found the Holy Lance, took Jerusalem and founded the Latin Kingdom of Jerusalem.

name: Second Crusade
description: Crusade after the fall of Edessa in 1144 that accomplished little besides the capture of Lisbon.

name: Third Crusade
description: Crusade led by Frederick Barbarossa, Philip II and Richard I after Saladin recaptured Jerusalem.

name: Fourth Crusade
description: 1204 crusade diverted by the Venetians to sack Constantinople, sealing the East-West division.

name: Albigensian Crusade
description: Crusade against the Cathars in Southern France declared by Innocent III in 1209.

name: Inquisition
description: Church institution whose founding soon follows the Albigensian crusade.

name: Pope Zacharias
description: Eighth-century pope who allied with Pepin the Short.

name: Pepin the Short
description: Frankish ruler who restored the pope to power over the Papal States.

name: Charlemagne
description: Son of Pepin crowned Holy Roman Emperor in 800, strengthening Western Europe.

name: Papal States
description: Territories over which Pepin restored papal power.

name: Constantinople
description: Seat of the Eastern patriarchate, sacked by the Fourth Crusade in 1204.

name: Byzantium
description: The Eastern Christian empire, separated from the Latin Church and now reluctantly under a Western patriarch.

name: Treaty of Verdun
description: 843 treaty dividing the Frankish empire.

name: Great Schism
description: The schism between Latin and Greek Churches, complete by about 1054.

name: Frederick II
description: New emperor who promised to lead another crusade from Germany.

name: Franciscans
description: Order of friars founded by Francis preaching poverty and living by charity in towns.

name: Dominicans
description: Order of friars founded by Dominic to combat heresy, with chapters at Paris, Bologna, Rome.

name: St. Thomas Aquinas
description: Theologian who will write the Summa Theologiae later in the thirteenth century.

name: Summa Theologiae
description: Theological work by Thomas Aquinas to be written later in the 13th century.

name: Dante
description: Author of the Divine Comedy, to be written later in the thirteenth century.

name: Divine Comedy
description: Dante's great medieval work, not yet written in 1220.

name: Excommunication
description: Declaration that a sinner has left the Church, losing sacramental benefits and Faith Points; also called Anathema.

name: Interdict
description: A form of excommunication excluding an entire area from the sacraments, reducing the Dominion by 1 each year.

name: Sacraments
description: Seven holy ceremonies with supernatural effects that often impart Faith Points and only affect willing participants.

name: Faith Points
description: Points used as if the character had True Faith, granted by sacraments and relics, spent like Confidence.

name: True Faith
description: Holy Virtue granting a Faith Score and Magic Resistance; Christian magi may possess it.

name: Confidence
description: Points spent to bolster rolls; penance grants a Confidence Point.

name: Baptism
description: Sacrament cleansing original sin, driving away possessing spirits and canceling non-Divine supernatural effects; baptismal names cannot be True Names.

name: Confirmation
description: Sacrament in which a Christian receives the Holy Spirit, granting a Faith Point.

name: Marriage
description: Sacrament joining two people against temptation, granting both a Faith Point and a holy connection.

name: Penance
description: Sacrament of confession and absolution that grants a Confidence Point and a holy connection to the confessor.

name: The Eucharist
description: The most sacred sacrament, turning bread and wine into Christ's body and blood; grants a Faith Point.

name: Ordination
description: Sacrament of joining holy orders, granting a Faith Point and spiritual authority over an aura.

name: Extreme Unction
description: Last Rites absolving mortal sins and protecting the soul from supernatural powers for three days after death.

name: True Name
description: A name usable for magical purposes; baptismal names cannot serve as True Names.

name: Holy Connection
description: A sacramental bond between people (godparents, confessor, bishop) that some holy powers can affect.

name: Purgatory
description: Temporary state of punishment for penitent sinners, reachable through gateways, associated by theologians with the Divine Realm.

name: Hell
description: Permanent place of punishment for those who reject God completely.

name: Heaven
description: God's kingdom, home of the saints.

name: King John
description: King of England whose rebellion against the Church led to the 1208 interdict.

name: England
description: Kingdom placed under interdict in 1208.

name: Nicene Creed
description: Early Christian creed (325 A.D.); the Latin addition of 'filioque' was a point of East-West dispute.

name: Original Sin
description: Sinfulness inherited from the Fall of Adam and Eve, cleansed by baptism.

name: Venial Sin
description: Light sins committed daily that add to time in Purgatory.

name: Mortal Sin
description: Grave sin removing a person from the state of grace, requiring penance and absolution.

name: Seven Deadly Sins
description: Pride, Wrath, Envy, Sloth, Lust, Gluttony and Avarice, the 'capital vices' leading to mortal sin.

name: Seven Capital Virtues
description: Four cardinal virtues (Wisdom, Temperance, Courage, Justice) and three theological virtues (Faith, Hope, Charity).

name: St. Gregory
description: Called the deadly sins the 'capital vices'.

name: Plato
description: Ancient philosopher from whom the cardinal virtues derive.

name: Adam and Eve
description: First humans whose Fall is the source of original sin.

name: Fasting
description: Usual act of penance: one meal a day, abstaining from meat and wine, typically for forty days.

name: Roman Penitential
description: Halitgar's penitential listing penances for magical and sacrilegious acts.

name: Halitgar
description: Author of the Roman Penitential.

name: Penitentials
description: Reference books for confessors listing appropriate penances for sinful acts.

name: Sortes Sanctorum
description: Divinatory oracles whose use the Roman Penitential punishes.

name: Trial by Ordeal
description: Court procedure invoking God's intervention to prove innocence; churchmen barred from it in 1215.

name: Test of the Cold Water
description: Most common ordeal: the accused is thrown into water and floats if innocent.

name: Judgment of the Glowing Iron
description: Ordeal of carrying red-hot iron; innocent if wounds are uninfected after three days.

name: Test of the Boiling Water
description: Ordeal of removing a stone from a boiling cauldron.

name: Ordeal of the Bier
description: Ordeal in murder cases where the victim bleeds if the guilty touches the body.

name: Trial by Combat
description: Ordeal where accused and accuser fight; rare in 1220, seen only in lands of Saxon heritage.

name: Ordeal of the Cross
description: Ordeal where both parties hold arms outstretched before the cross; first to drop loses.

name: Just Temper
description: A temper of the Dominion that could favor the innocent in ordeals.

name: Relic
description: Minor General Virtue most commonly conferring finger bones or True Cross fragments.

name: Relics
description: Holy remains and objects with Faith Points and Divine Might; saints' remains are disseminated throughout Mythic Europe.

name: Fragments of the True Cross
description: Common relics with 1 Faith Point and Divine Might 10.

name: Bones of St Martin
description: Healing relics at the Church of St Martin in Tours with Faith 4 and Divine Might 40.

name: Church of St Martin
description: Church at Tours housing the bones of St Martin, a pilgrimage site for healing.

name: Tours
description: French city where St Martin was bishop and is entombed.

name: Mantle of Nerius
description: Mantle made by Verditius magus Ceylan for Nerius, letting the wearer survive without food; Faith 3, Divine Might 30; now lost.

name: Nerius
description: Criamon magus who reconciled his power with God and became St Nerius, patron saint of Christian magi (Divine Might 50), martyred at Fudarus in 1039.

name: Ceylan
description: Verditius magus, amicus of Nerius, who gave him his mantle.

name: House Verditius
description: Hermetic House of Ceylan, maker of the Mantle of Nerius.

name: Valoran
description: Disciple of Nerius who inherited the mantle and then disappeared.

name: The Holy Lance
description: Spear of Longinus found by the First Crusade in 1098 and lost in 1101; Faith 7, Divine Might 70, can invoke Celestial Immunity on ten people.

name: Longinus
description: Roman soldier who pierced Christ's side with a spear.

name: Pilate
description: Roman governor petitioned to break the legs of the crucified.

name: Waldensians
description: Heretical followers of Peter Waldo, declared heretics in 1184 for Donatism.

name: Peter Waldo
description: Wealthy Lyon merchant who gave away his wealth in the late 1100s and founded the Waldensians.

name: Donatism
description: Ancient heresy that sacraments are invalid when performed by unworthy priests.

name: Cathars
description: Dualist heretics (Albigensians) localized in Languedoc, distinguishing perfecti from followers and practicing the consolamentum.

name: Manichaeism
description: Older dualist heresy resembling Catharism.

name: Perfecti
description: Cathar men and women striving to overcome their physical bodies to become perfect spiritual beings.

name: Consolamentum
description: Cathar ritual laying on of hands substituted for sacraments.

name: Pater Noster
description: The 'Our Father', later called the Lord's Prayer, recited by Cathars.

name: Languedoc
description: Region where the Cathars were localized.

name: Lyon
description: City of Peter Waldo; St Guinefort is venerated in a diocese there.

name: Maurillac
description: Where seven Waldensians were executed in 1214.

name: Bishop of Toul
description: Ordered all Waldensians chained and tried in 1192.

name: King of Aragon
description: Banished the Waldensians from his lands in 1194.

name: Heresy
description: Belief conflicting with established Church teaching, corrected and ultimately punished by burning.

name: Secular Clergy
description: Clergy administering to human society from within it (bishops, priests, deacons).

name: Regular Clergy
description: Clergy bound by a Rule and divided into orders, living removed from society.

name: Bishop
description: Clergyman with spiritual authority over a diocese, able to confirm, ordain, excommunicate and pronounce interdict.

name: Archbishop
description: Bishop of a very important city overseeing other bishops in a region.

name: Pope
description: Bishop of Rome, successor of Peter with spiritual authority over Christendom.

name: Cardinals
description: Papal advisers who elect the pope's successor.

name: Legates
description: Personal representatives of the pope sent throughout Europe.

name: Parish Priest
description: Priest overseeing a parish and performing its sacraments.

name: Deacon
description: Cleric below the priest who looks after Church funds and assists in the Eucharist.

name: Subdeacon
description: Assists the deacon with the implements of the Mass.

name: Minor Orders
description: Clerks such as porters, lectors, exorcists and acolytes who need not be ordained.

name: Diocese
description: Area under a bishop's spiritual authority.

name: Parish
description: Smallest unit of a diocese, often the size of a manor.

name: Canons
description: Cathedral administrative staff who elect a new bishop.

name: Bishop of Bayeux
description: Bishop who wielded a mace at the Battle of Hastings.

name: Archbishop Turpin
description: Heroic figure from The Song of Roland.

name: The Song of Roland
description: Epic featuring Archbishop Turpin.

name: St. Peter
description: Chief apostle and first bishop of Rome, greater saint (Divine Might 75) and patron of the Church, popes, and fishermen.

name: Exorcism
description: Christian rite costing a Confidence or Faith point that helps a possessed person break free of infernal influence.

name: Adjuration
description: Holy tradition effects that achieve immediate results against possession.

name: Roman Ritual
description: Instructions for performing exorcism.

name: Monasteries
description: Self-sufficient religious houses governed by a Rule, dominated by an abbey church.

name: Rule of St. Benedict
description: Rule established by Benedict governing monastic life of opus Dei, lectio divina and opus manuum.

name: St. Benedict of Nursia
description: Founder of the monastic Rule; area saint and patron of Europe, monks, and farm workers.

name: Benedictines
description: Monastic houses of men and women following Benedict's Rule.

name: Decadence
description: Fat golden demon with heavy chains and a giant mouth, dressed as a monk.

name: Sodomy
description: Wiry clawed demonic spirit, part human and part wolf, dressed as a monk.

name: Apathy
description: Cold insubstantial faceless shadow demon dressed as a monk.

name: The Offices
description: The monastic day of hours: Matins, Lauds, Prime, Terce, Sext, Nones, Vespers, Compline.

name: Abbot
description: Elected head of a monastery, often of social status similar to bishops.

name: Abbess
description: Head of a convent.

name: Prior
description: Chief assistant chosen by the abbot.

name: Cellarer
description: Monk in charge of temporal affairs of the house.

name: Chapter
description: All the monks gathered for official business; elects the abbot.

name: Cluny
description: Monastery founded in 910 that led the Cluniac Order.

name: Cluniac Order
description: Benedictine reform emphasizing worship and freedom from noble control.

name: Citeaux
description: Founded in 1098, origin of the Cistercian Order.

name: Cistercian Order
description: Twelfth-century reform returning to Benedict's Rule, poverty and isolation.

name: Orthodox Church
description: Eastern Greek Church following the Eastern patriarch's liturgy.

name: St. John of Damascus
description: Greatest Eastern theologian (670s-760s), outlined Orthodox Christianity.

name: Blessed Virgin Mary
description: Mother of Christ, most venerated saint with Divine Might 100, entombed in Ephesus.

name: Iconoclastic Controversy
description: Quarrel from the 700s in Byzantium over veneration of icons.

name: St. Basil of Caesarea
description: Author of the single Rule governing Byzantine monasteries.

name: Filioque
description: 'And the Son' added by the West to the Nicene Creed, a cause of schism.

name: Eastern Patriarch
description: Head of the Eastern Church.

name: Militant Orders
description: Orders of warrior monks established to aid the crusades; four major ones in 1220.

name: Knights Hospitaller
description: Knights Hospitaller of St. John in Jerusalem, following the Rule of St. Augustine, approved 1113.

name: Knights Templar
description: Order of Poor Knights of the Temple of Solomon, founded c. 1119, bankers said to practice secret mysteries.

name: Order of Santiago
description: Iberian crusading order founded 1170 by Ferdinand II of Leon, involved in the Reconquista.

name: Teutonic Knights
description: Order of the Hospital of Saint Mary of the Teutons of Jerusalem, founded 1190, militarized 1198.

name: Council of Troyes
description: 1128 council at which the Templars received their Rule.

name: Ferdinand II of Leon
description: Founded the Order of Santiago in 1170.

name: Reconquista
description: Re-conquering of the Iberian peninsula from Muslim invaders.

name: St. James the Great
description: Apostle of Compostela; greater saint, patron of Spain, pilgrims, laborers.

name: Acre
description: Where the Teutonic Knights served as a Hospitaller order.

name: Seljuk Turks
description: Militant Turks who occupied Baghdad and seized Jerusalem.

name: Manzikert
description: Where the Turks routed the Byzantine army in 1071.

name: Nicea
description: City reached by Turks and recaptured by crusaders.

name: Antioch
description: City conquered by crusaders, where the holy lance was discovered.

name: Latin Kingdom of Jerusalem
description: Crusader kingdom established on Christmas Day 1100.

name: Edessa
description: Crusader city whose fall in 1144 triggered the Second Crusade.

name: Saladin
description: Saracen leader who recaptured Jerusalem in 1187.

name: Frederick Barbarossa
description: Monarch who drowned en route in the Third Crusade.

name: Philip II of France
description: Monarch who fell ill and returned from the Third Crusade.

name: Richard I of England
description: Negotiated a truce allowing pilgrims into Jerusalem.

name: Venetians
description: Diverted the Fourth Crusade to Constantinople.

name: Universities
description: Studia generalia of masters and students organized like guilds with four faculties.

name: University of Paris
description: Prominent university known for theology and liberal arts.

name: University of Bologna
description: University known for law and emerging medicine.

name: Oxford
description: English university gaining note for mathematics.

name: Salamanca
description: Spanish city with a newly established university.

name: Friars
description: Mendicant orders (Dominican and Franciscan) calling for poverty in service to the Church.

name: Dominic
description: Founder of the Dominican order to combat heresy.

name: Francis
description: Son of an Italian cloth merchant who founded the Franciscans in 1210.

name: Sentences
description: Peter the Lombard's four-book theology textbook; Divine Lore and Theology summae, Quality 9.

name: Peter the Lombard
description: Author of the Sentences (c.1100-1160).

name: The City of God
description: St Augustine's tractatus on Church Lore (Quality 12).

name: Consolations of Philosophy
description: Boethius' tractatus on Philosophiae (Quality 9).

name: Boethius
description: Author of Consolations of Philosophy (480-525).

name: The Celestial Hierarchy
description: Summa on Dominion Lore describing the nine angelic choirs, attributed to Dionysius the Areopagite.

name: Dionysius the Areopagite
description: Greek convert of St Paul believed to have written The Celestial Hierarchy.

name: Theology
description: Academic Ability taught by the Bible and the Sentences.

name: Church Lore
description: Lore Ability taught by the Bible and The City of God.

name: Dominion Lore
description: Ability taught by The Celestial Hierarchy.

name: Divine Lore
description: Ability taught by Book I of the Sentences.

name: Philosophiae
description: Academic Ability taught by Consolations of Philosophy.

name: Saints
description: Holy dead accepted into heaven who intercede and grant miracles; greater, area and local saints.

name: Cult of Saints
description: Popular veneration of saints through feasts, pilgrimages and relics.

name: Canonization
description: Process by which the Church declares a saint, now decided by the pope.

name: The Golden Legend
description: Jacobus de Voragine's authoritative saints' lives, written around 1260.

name: Jacobus de Voragine
description: Author of The Golden Legend.

name: Patron Saint
description: The saint most familiar to a person or place, to whom petitions are addressed.

name: Invoking a Saint
description: Daily Communication + Charm roll asking a saint for a miracle.

name: Threatening a Saint
description: 'Humiliation of a saint': Presence + Leadership roll forcing a miracle after a failed invocation, risking curses.

name: Divine Might
description: Measure of a Divine being's or relic's power.

name: Magic Resistance
description: Protection from supernatural powers; some saintly powers grant it.

name: Saints' Miracles
description: Supernatural deeds performed by saints expressed as powers channelled from God.

name: Acknowledgment of Evil
description: Saint power forcing any demon in voice range to declare its Infernal nature.

name: Apparition
description: Saint power creating a physical but invulnerable manifestation of the saint.

name: Celestial Immunity
description: Saint power making the recipient immune to physical damage while the threat lasts.

name: Cure Blindness
description: Saint power permanently restoring sight.

name: Expel Demons
description: Saint power expelling a demon back to Hell, like Demon's Eternal Oblivion.

name: Grant of Serenity
description: Saint power calming a petitioner and nullifying malign Mentem spells.

name: Mass Healing
description: Saint power healing a crowd of all diseases and wounds.

name: Raise the Dead
description: Saint power restoring life to a corpse whose soul is not in heaven.

name: Resist Temptation
description: Saint power granting Magic Resistance against demonic temptation.

name: Sanctuary of Virginity
description: Saint power miraculously protecting a follower's virginity.

name: Scourging of Snakes
description: Saint power expelling all snakes from an island up to the size of Ireland.

name: Straighten the Crippled
description: Saint power healing the lame and deformed.

name: The Dutiful Shepherd
description: Saint power sending an image of the saint to lead a lost petitioner to safety.

name: The Faithful Made Whole
description: Saint power curing all disease and physical wounds.

name: The Incombustible Shroud
description: Saint power rendering the target immune to fire.

name: The Laborer's Boon
description: Saint power mending or replacing a broken tool.

name: The Leap of the Faithful
description: Saint power instantly transporting a person any distance.

name: Tomorrow's Bounty
description: Saint power creating food for a large crowd.

name: Blindness
description: Saint curse permanently blinding the target.

name: Blisters of Humility
description: Saint curse covering the target with boils for a week.

name: Dysenteric Infliction
description: Saint curse destroying the target with fatal dysentery.

name: Flabbergast the Impertinent
description: Saint curse casting the target into a loud, exhausting night's sleep.

name: Humility of Caesar
description: Saint curse throwing a rider from his horse or felling him on his face.

name: Ignis Domini
description: 'The Fire of God', a saint curse bringing a pillar of fire from heaven (+30 damage).

name: Rebuke the Unfaithful
description: Saint curse threatening death within thirty days unless the target mends his ways.

name: Smiting of the Lord
description: Saint curse hurling a lightning bolt for +35 damage.

name: Swallowed Alive and Sent to Hell
description: Saint curse opening a chasm that drops the target into Hell.

name: Terrify the Unbeliever
description: Saint curse making the target flee in terror until dawn.

name: The Earth's Riches
description: Saint power turning sticks and stones into gold and gems.

name: The Feast of Worms
description: Saint curse infesting the target's body with maggots.

name: Demon's Eternal Oblivion
description: Hermetic spell to which the Expel Demons power is compared.

name: Enchantment of Detachment
description: Hermetic Mentem spell similar to Grant of Serenity.

name: Touch of Midas
description: Hermetic spell whose value comparison is used for The Earth's Riches.

name: Vim
description: Hermetic Form used to classify saints' powers and curses.

name: Imaginem
description: Hermetic Form used to classify saints' powers and curses.

name: Corpus
description: Hermetic Form used to classify saints' powers and curses.

name: Mentem
description: Hermetic Form used to classify saints' powers and curses.

name: Animal
description: Hermetic Form used to classify saints' powers and curses.

name: Ignem
description: Hermetic Form used to classify saints' powers and curses.

name: Terram
description: Hermetic Form used to classify saints' powers and curses.

name: Herbam
description: Hermetic Form used to classify saints' powers and curses.

name: Auram
description: Hermetic Form used to classify saints' powers and curses.

name: Greater Saint
description: Saints of Divine Might 75, typically apostles or Church fathers, venerated throughout Mythic Europe.

name: Area Saint
description: Saints of Divine Might about 50 venerated over large areas.

name: Local Saint
description: Saints of Divine Might 25 venerated by a town or two.

name: St Joseph
description: Elderly widower to whom Mary was bequeathed.

name: Angel Gabriel
description: Angel who told Mary she would conceive the Son of God.

name: Angel Michael
description: Angel whose aid St Nerius asked to resist the vision of the Enigma.

name: Ephesus
description: City where Mary spent her last days and where her tomb is.

name: Nazareth
description: Mary's hometown.

name: Bethlehem
description: Where Mary delivered Jesus.

name: Herod
description: Persecutor from whom Mary and family fled to Egypt.

name: St Ambrose
description: Wrote that Mary first saw the Resurrection; greater saint, patron of bishops, learning and bees.

name: Simon Magus
description: Sorcerer in Nero's employ whose demons St Peter dispelled.

name: Nero
description: Emperor who crucified Peter.

name: St Martin of Tours
description: Soldier turned bishop of Tours; area saint (Divine Might 50), patron of soldiers, horses and beggars.

name: Amiens
description: Where Martin gave his cloak to a beggar.

name: Arian Heresy
description: Heresy St Martin combated.

name: St Guinefort
description: A greyhound venerated as a local saint (Divine Might 25), patron of protecting local children.

name: Criamon
description: Hermetic House to which St Nerius belonged.

name: Enigma
description: Criamon mystery Nerius discovered in a secret Alpine well.

name: Provencal Tribunal
description: Tribunal where St Nerius was born.

name: Normandy Tribunal
description: Tribunal meeting of 1039 during which St Nerius was martyred.

name: Fudarus
description: Domus Magnus of House Tytalus, where St Nerius was martyred.

name: House Tytalus
description: Hermetic House whose domus magnus is Fudarus; its magi joined the attack on Nerius.

name: House Tremere
description: Hermetic House whose magi declared a Wizard's March against St Nerius.

name: House Flambeau
description: Hermetic House whose wizards joined the martyrdom of Nerius.

name: Wizard's March
description: Hermetic sentence of death declared against St Nerius.

name: Certamen
description: Hermetic magical duel; St Nerius never lost a match.

name: Vis
description: Magical resource; St Nerius could cure the sick without it.

name: Arcadia
description: Realm St Nerius is said to protect.

name: Durenmar
description: Covenant whose Great Library holds St Nerius' autobiographical scrolls.

name: Great Library of Durenmar
description: Library holding twelve scrolls of St Nerius' travels.

name: St Andrew
description: Greater saint, patron of Scotland, fishermen, and sailors.

name: St Matthew
description: Greater saint, patron of tax collectors and bankers.

name: St Thomas
description: Greater saint, patron of India, architects and surveyors.

name: St Jude
description: Greater saint, patron of lost causes.

name: St Jerome
description: Greater saint, patron of scholars.

name: St Edward the Confessor
description: Area saint, patron of England.

name: St Patrick
description: Area saint, patron of Ireland.

name: St Thomas a Becket
description: Area saint, patron of Canterbury.

name: St Denis
description: Area saint, patron of Paris.

name: St Boniface
description: Area saint, patron of Germany, brewers and tailors.

name: St Wenceslaus
description: Area saint, patron of Bohemia.

name: St Finnbarr
description: Local saint, patron of Cork.

name: St Gilbert
description: Local saint, patron of Sempringham.

name: St Godric
description: Local saint, patron of Durham and Finchale.

name: St David of Thessalonike
description: Local saint, patron of Thessalonike.

name: St Kevin
description: Local saint, patron of Dublin.

name: St Eulogius
description: Local saint, patron of Cordoba.

name: St Irene
description: Local saint, patron of Thessalonica.

name: St Gotthard
description: Local saint, patron of Hildesheim.

name: St Adalbert
description: Local saint, patron of Prague.

name: Adalbero, Bishop of Laon
description: Author of the Poem to King Robert (c.1025) on the three orders of society.

name: Book of Solomon
description: Book whose copies teach the Notory Art.

name: Rings of Solomon
description: Orations recited through Ars Notoria.

name: Ars Notoria (Virtue)
description: Major Hermetic/Supernatural Virtue granting Ars Notoria 1, requiring scores of 4 in Artes Liberales and four languages.

name: Holy Music (Virtue)
description: Major Supernatural Method Virtue granting Holy Music 1.

name: Holy Music
description: Supernatural Ability like Meditation gaining divine insight through music, taught by the Cantores.

name: Cantores
description: Holy tradition that primarily teaches Holy Music.

name: Senior Clergy
description: Major Social Status Virtue: presbyter, archpriest, bishop, or abbot with spiritual authority and Reputation 4.

name: Brother Chaplain
description: Minor Social Status: a priest of a crusading order answerable only to the pope.

name: Brother Knight
description: Minor Social Status: a knight of a crusading order sworn to obedience, poverty, and chastity.

name: Brother Sergeant
description: Minor Social Status: non-knight member of a crusading order.

name: Eastern Priest
description: Minor Status Virtue like Priest but without required celibacy.

name: Priest
description: Minor Social Status Virtue prerequisite for Senior Clergy.

name: Monastic Vows (Hermetic)
description: Major Hermetic Flaw; Monastic Vows can prerequisite Senior Clergy.

name: Excommunicate
description: Major Story Flaw: cast out of the Church, bad Reputation 3, no sacramental benefits.

name: Pagan
description: Major Story and Supernatural Flaw introduced among Christian Flaws.

name: Unbaptised
description: Major Story Flaw among the new Christian Flaws.

name: Failed Monk
description: Minor Status Flaw: cast out of a cloistered order, poor Reputation 2; Failed Nun for women.

name: Wealthy
description: Major Virtue that combined with Senior Clergy places one among the wealthiest.

name: Temporal Influence
description: Virtue that with Senior Clergy means controlling an influential diocese or abbey.

name: Artes Liberales
description: Academic Ability required at 4 for Ars Notoria.

name: Magister in Artibus
description: Social Status allowing Ars Notoria at character creation.

name: Clerk
description: Social Status allowing Ars Notoria at character creation.

name: Tribunal
description: Hermetic assembly where magi bring charges.

name: Holy Spirit
description: Third person of the Trinity received at Confirmation.

name: Holy Roman Empire
description: Empire whose emperor Charlemagne was crowned; an area of saint veneration.

name: Holy Land
description: Region the Crusades sought to regain from Muslims.

name: Saracens
description: Muslim invaders of Europe.
